title: Cratylus keeps no ledger: the work is shown by version control, the harness and the lead's outcomes
situation: The operator: retire the ledger. What is in flight and how it ended is what the project's version control and the lead's outcome already show; what work cost is what the harness records and the outcome reports. The project's record was one event store of two streams, the journal for the design and the ledger for the work.
decision: The concept journal is the project's one record of its own: its design, every context's meaning and every decision, each entry naming its context, owned by the architect, only appended, every view computed from it. What work is in flight and how it ended is what the project's version control and the lead's outcomes show; what work cost against its estimate is what the harness records and the outcome reports. Cratylus keeps no ledger and no record or view of the work of its own, captures nothing of agent runs, and writes nothing about the work into the repository apart from the work itself. The ledger's earlier files are deleted, with nothing migrated. The examples and their checks are documents kept beside the journal, changed like any other work. Bounded contexts are a field of the journal's entries, never separate stores.
consequences: The ledger leaves the design and the product: its capability, command, tool, capture of agent runs, files and every mention in what cratylus delivers go. Reconstitution, context overview, efficiency, outcome and the concept journal state where the work is seen instead.
